entries.subject: vista-infrared shipped image lens
entries.finding: Shipped lens, now recolouring the finite-emission model a9e2048a… with its own fitted tone curve (result f6323093…). Registration unchanged: 5340 held-out matches qualify it inside its matched hull; exterior placement is extrapolated. After the tone fit its analytic render is still 16.6% brighter than its own image (hue error 5.70°), because every lens shares the one opacity fitted to Horálek; a per-lens opacity scale would be needed. Earlier finding (2026-09-14, repaint delivery): Default ESO Y/J/Ks display, 8954 by 10000 pixels, repaints the existing simulated density without changing geometry or alpha. The 5340 held-out matches qualify relative registration inside its matched hull; exterior placement is extrapolated.

entries.subject: horalek-widefield shipped image lens
entries.finding: Default lens and the image the finite-emission model a9e2048a… was fitted to (result cab541ef…, tone-fitted). Registration unchanged: 198 held-out matches over a 60.2 percent hull; extended placement is extrapolated. After the tone fit its analytic render is 1.8% brighter than its own image with a 3.76° hue error. Earlier finding (2026-09-14, repaint delivery): Horálek visible-light photograph, 6582 by 4388 pixels, with acquisition instrument/bands unresolved. The 198 held-out matches qualify relative registration over a 60.2 percent hull. Exact density/alpha and the shared catalogue remain fixed; extended placement is extrapolated.

entries.subject: wise-wide-infrared shipped image lens
entries.finding: Shipped lens, now recolouring the finite-emission model a9e2048a… with its own fitted tone curve (result 6223c6cd…). Its fixed WCS check is unchanged. After the tone fit its analytic render is still 264% brighter than its own image (hue error 8.14°): its composite spans about 19 grey levels inside its footprint and the curve is pinned at its floor under the shared opacity, so a per-lens opacity scale would be needed. Earlier finding (2026-09-14, repaint delivery): NASA/IPAC AllWISE W4/W2/W1 color HiPS mosaic, 6000² pixels across 24 degrees. Its fixed WCS passed 34,811 independently retrieved AllWISE W1 matches without fitting a transform. This validates W1 geometry, not diffuse photometry, visible seams or simulated gas depth.

entries.subject: Garver et al. simulated stellar density
entries.finding: The same Garver et al. simulation is now the shape hypothesis of the finite-emission model: its depth distribution carries the envelope (80.75% of the Horálek light) and its strongest ray mode places each of the 470 fitted components. It is not observed gas or dust density, and no LMC depth tracer is in this repository to test it. Earlier finding (2026-09-14, repaint delivery): The existing full-density simulation supplies cloud support, not observed gas/dust density. Candidate images repaint its exact geometry and alpha; the common image-to-model placement is a display fit, not a particle-to-star identification.

entries.subject: Bonanos 2009 massive-star catalogue
entries.finding: 1,042 stars with finite V <= 16 on covered Horálek footprint pixels are placed by the finite-model star layer: each depth inverts the joint emission x simulation density x (1+z/D)^2 CDF at a fixed per-star quantile. 39 rows the former 3x placement swallowed fall outside the true footprint. Brightest-40 stars against the registered image: 17 within 1 px, median 1.19 px (22.9 arcsec), mirrored control 1 of 40. No individual distances are measured. Earlier finding (2026-09-14, repaint delivery, 943 stars): Measured J2000 sky positions and Johnson V <= 16 inside the SMASH footprint select 943 stars. A deterministic joint cloud-emission and stellar-density prior assigns depth along each ray; no individual distances or proper-motion propagation are measured by this preparation.

entries.subject: SMASH noirlab2030a sky frame
entries.finding: The original SMASH publisher frame remains the image-registration and stellar-selection reference. The former photo-colored lens and parametric source recipe are historical; their retained source.jpg is a publisher AstroPix derivative, not a local observation.

entries.subject: Native NOX plus classical residual baseline
entries.finding: Pinned native source removal and the earlier positive compact-residual union supply starless color inputs. Exact RGB recombination and unchanged pixels outside masks qualify accounting only; crowded blends and intrinsic knots remain ambiguous.

entries.subject: Three-lens 2026-09-09 handoff
entries.finding: Superseded by the finite-emission promotion: the three lenses ship with identity appearance controls, and each lens's correction is its fitted tone curve inside the result identity; the new receipt pins the three result ids. Earlier finding (2026-09-14): The saved browser handoff pins VISTA, Horálek and WISE result identities and authored appearance controls. Existing delivery byte targets make restoration reviewable; this 2026-09-14 documentation audit is not a new cold-cache replay or material acceptance.

entries.subject: DSS2 24-degree optical comparison
entries.finding: Survey-WCS display preview retains plate seams, foreground stars and uneven backgrounds; it was not processed as a cloud.
entries.revisitWhen: Qualify native photometry/background and independent registration with usable diffuse coverage before any processing.

entries.subject: SMASH team wider mosaic
entries.finding: The 4111 by 5000 author mosaic has 6887 held-out star checks but only its central 30 percent is qualified. Black fields are missing observations, seams remain and image-specific rights are not declared.
entries.revisitWhen: Resolve reuse terms and outer-field registration/masks before adopting the wider source.

entries.subject: Ciel Austral optical/line-enhanced image
entries.finding: The 14400 by 14200 author image has a 74.1 percent matched hull and detailed central structure but no open reuse licence was found; APOD credits author copyright. It remains a comparison.
entries.revisitWhen: Obtain derivative-compatible permission and qualify all intended footprint/processing before inclusion.

entries.subject: Naztronomy mosaic preview
entries.finding: The acquired 3074 by 3163 author preview is smaller than the unavailable advertised high-resolution version. RGB versus dual-narrowband labeling remains ambiguous; no open reuse licence was identified.
entries.revisitWhen: Acquire a usable original with explicit derivative permission, band/processing history and qualified astrometry.

entries.subject: Historical SMASH broad/filled/photo-conditioned volumes
entries.finding: The full-photo and connected-component depth trials retained photographic edges, thick-sheet side views and sampling streaks after their bounded loop. Front-ray agreement and repeatability did not override the failed morphology gate.
entries.revisitWhen: Revisit only with a source/depth hypothesis that improves the same fixed-camera failures while preserving qualified support and stellar positions.

entries.subject: Starlet, median and getsf comparisons
entries.finding: Automatic sparse masks did not pass production morphology. The official getsf full-crop run reached its 30-minute bound without final component maps; adapter tests and installation were verified separately and do not constitute a completed scientific comparison.
entries.revisitWhen: Complete a bounded same-native-crop comparison with actual valid outputs and assess connected morphology; preserve signed residuals and uncalibrated display-unit caveats.

entries.subject: Broader shape masks and profile-threshold trials
entries.finding: Stronger minimum-width settings improved compact-light removal, but broader shape/mask variants introduced dark patches and were rejected. Raising profile thresholds increased zero-covariance cores; exact accounting alone did not make the diffuse target star-free.
entries.revisitWhen: A revised removal method must preserve adjacent extended emission and original-source accounting while visibly reducing blends/halos without dark patches.

entries.subject: Wrong-cloud fixed-benchmark repaint
entries.finding: The 416-slice historical painter selected an old photo-derived cloud and removed the saved Alignment fit. Internal projection checks passed while the cross-tab view was wrong; the current density repaint supersedes that ownership error.
entries.revisitWhen: Do not restore this route; any alternative must identify the actual shared cloud and pass independent cross-tab geometry/registration checks.

entries.subject: Historical smooth-density and sampling calibration
entries.finding: The earlier 309-quad density route changed the viewed cloud. Physical pitch and quantization feedback improved integrated energy but all strict browser handoff comparisons still failed; further sampling reached an impasse.
entries.revisitWhen: Reopen only at the common encoding/compositing owner with identical-camera evidence, fixed intended density support and no per-image gain fitting.

entries.subject: Current XYZ handoff brightness/banding limits
entries.finding: The repaint banks whose handoff failed are retired. The finite-emission bank paints all three axes from one fitted neutral alpha and fades faint texels to neutral below alpha 11, and the app inspection shows no bank banding at Earth, oblique or either 90° side view, but the dedicated XYZ handoff comparison has not been run on this bank. Earlier finding (2026-09-14): Current source-colored density uses shared geometry and alpha, but six historical dedicated handoff comparisons remained failed. Those numerical measurements belong to their recorded banks; successful later interaction checks do not establish rotation stability.
entries.revisitWhen: Run the unchanged same-camera bank-isolation gate on the actual candidate and fix the common material/compositing cause while preserving stars and local texture continuity.

entries.subject: Two-scale finite emission on the measured sky registration
entries.finding: Model a9e2048a… (recipe emission-envelope.json, exposure 2.418, alpha chroma limit 11) fits the registered, star-removed Horálek image: 470 components, projection RMSE 0.10458 -> 0.03247, total relative squared error 0.013060, envelope 80.75% of the light with 3.29% excess, all components on prior support. Placement is the identity, which reproduces the registered corners to 0.000 arcsec; the envelope keeps the simulation shape. materialGatePassed is false: the depth structure is a hypothesis.

entries.subject: Superseded alignment-density-material-v1 delivery
entries.finding: The previous LMC bank repainted one fixed simulated density with each registered image (144 slices per lens, 943 stars, VISTA default), constrained from the Earth-facing view only and placed on a hand-authored 3x display fit. Its 432 slices and 9 atlases leave the prepared inventory, its compact bake inputs and atlas mapping are removed, and the laboratory bake recipe no longer delivers to the application. Its source record, recipe and retained evidence stay as documents; its README at the last delivering revision keeps its account.
entries.revisitWhen: A future delivery needs a projection-only repaint again, or the retired record is shown to misstate its own inputs.

entries.subject: Regenerating the delivered bank from checked-in inputs
entries.finding: 6.6 MB of compact replay inputs regenerate the bank through prepare:nebulae. With the laboratory caches moved aside and prepared/ removed, all 726 regenerated slice textures are byte-identical to the promotion output, and the bank, its 9 atlases and the delivery receipt are byte-identical to the first restore; the lab-isolated application gate reproduces them too. The 13 prepared files are published to R2 and restore byte-identically through setup:prepared. The replay applies each lens tone curve; dropping it turns lmc-volume-lenses.test.mts red.

entries.subject: Application acceptance of the finite-emission bank
entries.finding: In the running application, reached by label fly-to: each lens decodes one texture at the Earth framing, a lens switch leaves the world camera unchanged, all 1,042 stars mount, render visible and toggle off, and the route raises no page error and no failing request. Earth, oblique and both exact 90-degree side views were inspected; the side views show line-of-sight extent rather than a sheet.

entries.subject: Per-lens opacity for VISTA and AllWISE
entries.finding: Every lens recolours one shared opacity fitted to Horálek, so a tone curve can only dim or recolour inside it. After fitting, VISTA stays 16.6% and AllWISE 264% brighter than their own images. Matching them needs a per-lens opacity scale, which gives up part of the one-geometry lens contract; not attempted here.
entries.revisitWhen: The lens contract admits a per-lens opacity scale, or a re-acquired AllWISE composite with a real stretch is registered.
